dedupe_keys.name: global shipping lanes major middle and minor sea routes georeferenced from the cia map of the world s oceans

description: This dataset gives a simple global network of shipping lanes as polylines, digitised from a published map so that sea routes can be drawn and analysed in GIS. It was created by the GitHub user newzealandpaul, who georeferenced the routes on the Central Intelligence Agency's Map of the World's Oceans (October 2012, held by the Library of Congress) and corrected problems in the original. Coverage: the world's oceans and main straits and canals. Each line carries a Type attribute of Major, Middle or Minor that roughly reflects the importance and traffic of the lane; there are no traffic volumes, dates or port links. Format and access: one GeoJSON file and one shapefile with example visualisations in a GitHub repository; free. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 with a custom clause that excludes Statista from the grant (the README also mentions share-alike, while the licence file is CC BY 4.0). Caveats: lanes follow a 2012 cartographic map, not observed vessel tracks, the classification is qualitative, and the data have not been updated since March 2022. Simulation uses: a lightweight maritime network for network flow and hazard exposure screening of shipping routes, such as chokepoint closures or storm tracks crossing major lanes. Related records: the World Bank Global Shipping Traffic Density (data-world-bank-global-shipping-traffic-density) gives observed AIS-based traffic, and searoute (model-searoute) computes sea routes between ports on a similar network.
